purpose: Keep routine development feedback fast while preserving a small, high-signal blocking suite and moving expensive broad campaigns to scheduled qualification.

routine_pr_and_pre_push: rustfmt and clippy with warnings denied
dependency metadata, unused-dependency, license, source, and ban checks
developer_feedback: local dev and test profiles use incremental compilation
the PR workflow installs only tools used by the PR profile
change.historical_evidence: The accepted M0-01 mutation baseline remains recorded for provenance, but it is not a recurring merge requirement.

detection_gained: a regression test proves the PR profile cannot accidentally invoke the scheduled coverage campaign
a regression test proves the extended profile still invokes coverage
routine feedback is fast enough to run on every push without bypass pressure
detection_lost: mutation score is no longer recomputed by automated profiles
cross-target compilation, full-history secret scanning, coverage, and Cargo Vet no longer run on every pull request
risk_controls: all product qualification and non-waivable release gates remain unchanged
the essential compile, lint, full-test, documentation, architecture, current-secret, dependency, and advisory checks remain blocking
scheduled extended failures remain explicit failures and cannot become qualification evidence
strict Rust lints, unsafe-code rejection, scaffold protection, and scope registration remain enforced

evidence.comparison: The authoritative local PR profile became 43.9 times faster, a 97.7 percent duration reduction. Dirty-tree evidence is diagnostic only; trusted clean CI remains the authority for merge eligibility.

dual_run: The old and new authoritative PR profiles were both executed successfully. Gate selection and dedicated regression tests verify that essential blocking checks remain active while scheduled checks stay outside the PR path.
